{"id":"persona-5s4b.60","title":"Trust bundle is seeded with an empty JWKS and a raw EC point as the X.509 authority, so no consumer can verify an issued JWT-SVID","description":"personad/src/main.rs:37-42 seeds the only trust bundle as:

    TrustBundle::new(
        TrustDomain::SshLocal,
        vec![signer.public_key_der().to_vec()],   // -> x509_authorities
        serde_json::json!({ "keys": [] }),        // -> jwt_authorities
    );

Two separate defects, one root cause -- the signing key is never published in a form any client can use.

(1) Empty JWKS. jwt_authorities is a literal {"keys": []}. service.rs:84-93 FetchJWTBundles serializes that value verbatim and returns it as the JWKS for trust domain ssh.local. Trigger: a consumer follows the standard SPIFFE Workload API flow -- FetchJWTBundles to get the verification keys, then verify the JWT-SVID from FetchJWTSVID. It gets zero keys, so every JWT-SVID the daemon issues is unverifiable. The daemon mints tokens no one can check. `persona trust-bundle list` (persona/src/main.rs:415-417) prints only a byte count, so this shows up as a plausible-looking "domain: ssh.local (jwks: 13 bytes)" rather than an obvious failure.

(2) Wrong type in x509_authorities. TrustBundle.x509_authorities is documented at persona-core/src/trust_bundle.rs:10-11 as "DER-encoded X.509 CA certificates". signer.public_key_der() (persona-core/src/signer.rs:178, 188) returns ring EcdsaKeyPair::public_key().as_ref(), which is the 65-byte uncompressed SEC1 point 0x04||X||Y -- not a certificate, not SubjectPublicKeyInfo, not DER at all (the field name public_key_der is itself misleading). service.rs:61-70 FetchX509Bundles concatenates these into the per-domain blob that the SPIFFE spec defines as concatenated ASN.1 DER certificates. Trigger: any conformant client calls FetchX509Bundles and tries to parse the result. It gets 65 bytes of raw curve point and fails to parse a certificate.

The e2e test reproduces the same empty-JWKS seeding at persona-grpc/tests/e2e.rs:220-224 instead of catching it, because it never fetches the bundle -- see the separate issue on that test verifying against its own in-process signer.

Fix direction: build a real JWKS (kid, kty EC, crv P-256, x/y from the point) for jwt_authorities, and leave x509_authorities empty until sign_x509_svid is implemented rather than filling it with a non-certificate.","status":"open","priority":0,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:59:09.316648563Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-13T20:59:09.316648563Z","labels":["correctness","review"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.60","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:59:09.332504362Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}
